h: Graves disease in a pregnant woman: drug class of choice?
p: Radioiodine is contraindicated in pregnancy; PTU is used in the first trimester (methimazole teratogenic), then methimazole later. Beta-blockers help symptoms short term.
Ultralarge vWF multimers cause platelet microthrombi: thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolysis (low haptoglobin), fever, renal and neurologic signs. Treat with plasma exchange.

h: Contralateral leg weakness with urinary incontinence and abulia: occluded artery?
p: ACA supplies the medial frontal and parietal lobes (leg motor and sensory cortex); stroke gives opposite leg weakness, incontinence, abulia. MCA stroke affects face and arm more.

h: Restlessness and pacing after starting fluphenazine: diagnosis?
p: Akathisia is the most common early extrapyramidal side effect of antipsychotics; treat by lowering the dose or adding propranolol or a benzodiazepine.

h: Same-sex fantasies with derogatory comments about same-sex couples: defense?
p: Reaction formation converts an unacceptable impulse into its exact opposite behavior (e.g., hostility toward what one secretly desires).

h: Crossbridge cycle: myosin detaches from actin when it binds what?
p: ATP binding releases the myosin head (rigor mortis occurs when ATP runs out); ATP hydrolysis then re-cocks the head. Calcium binds troponin C to expose myosin-binding sites.
Beta-lactams resemble the D-Ala-D-Ala terminus of peptidoglycan, blocking transpeptidase cross-linking. Sulfonamides mimic PABA/folate precursors.

h: Family history of flank pain, hematuria; now thunderclap headache with neck stiffness: cause?
p: ADPKD is associated with berry aneurysms; subarachnoid hemorrhage presents with 'worst headache of life' and meningismus. Diagnosis by noncontrast CT.

h: Ringed sideroblasts on marrow Prussian blue stain: deficient vitamin?
p: B6 is required for ALAS, the first step of heme synthesis; deficiency (isoniazid, alcohol) or lead causes sideroblastic anemia. Treat with pyridoxine.

h: Acetaminophen overdose: antidote that replenishes glutathione?
p: NAC restores glutathione to detoxify NAPQI and is most effective within 8 hours; use the Rumack-Matthew nomogram to guide therapy.

h: Octreotide mimics a hormone made by which cells?
p: Octreotide lowers splanchnic blood flow in variceal bleeding and treats carcinoid and acromegaly. G cells make gastrin and I cells make CCK.

x: keyed foreign-body site disputable (right main bronchus is classic)

h: Eczema, recurrent infections, high IgE and IgA, low IgM: associated finding?
p: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (WAS gene, X-linked): the triad of eczema, recurrent infections and thrombocytopenia with small platelets; treat with bone marrow transplant.

h: Mammillary body atrophy in a chronic alcoholic: which test is abnormal?
p: Thiamine is the cofactor of transketolase, pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase; Wernicke-Korsakoff shows mammillary body damage.

h: Genital tubercle gives rise to which female structure?
p: The genital tubercle forms the glans penis or clitoris; labioscrotal swellings form scrotum or labia majora; Bartholin glands correspond to bulbourethral glands.

x: keyed diagnosis (cyclothymia) not supported by depressive episodes shown

p: Cocaine blocks reuptake of norepinephrine, dopamine and serotonin, and is the only local anesthetic that causes vasoconstriction and euphoria.

h: Delirium tremens: when after the last drink is risk greatest?
p: Alcohol withdrawal: tremor and anxiety at 6-24 h, seizures at 12-48 h, delirium tremens at 48-96 h with autonomic instability; treat with benzodiazepines.

h: Rising BUN/creatinine with low urine sodium after aggressive diuresis: cause?
p: Prerenal azotemia: BUN:Cr over 20, FENa under 1 percent, urine osmolality over 500, and responds to volume repletion; ATN has muddy brown casts and high urine sodium.

h: Small molecule binding antibody but needing a carrier to be immunogenic?
p: Haptens (e.g., penicillin) trigger immune responses only when bound to carrier proteins; this underlies drug allergies.

h: Bullae and crepitus in a traumatic wound a week later: toxin?
p: Gas gangrene: alpha toxin (lecithinase/phospholipase C) causes myonecrosis and hemolysis; treat with debridement and penicillin plus clindamycin.
